verdicts.evidence: Every button has a working handler: Send invitation (514), Save name (365), row Remove (466), dialog Keep/Remove (532, 536), Try loading again (332), Try saving again (419), Invite again and Dismiss (562-573). Each calls the api or changes the view as labelled.
Lines 329, 341-349, 393: name, members, roles, last active, seat count and notifications all come from api.getTeam. No hardcoded figures or placeholder text; a missing lastActive shows 'Never' (472).
Lines 523-524: the remove confirmation names the person and the team in its title and states the consequence, so the decision carries the earlier context.

Each task is one or two inputs (invite: email and role, 158-167; rename: one field, 199-200); role and notification changes save at once. No task has about five inputs, several steps or long free text.

Line 165: invite role preselects Member, the lower privilege, and is reset to member after a send (503). Line 529: dialog focus starts on 'Keep on team'; the dialog has no form, so Enter does not remove.
A settings screen used now and then for six separate tasks (brief); no single frequent task dominates. All tasks are done in place apart from the remove confirmation.

Sections are members with invite (149-192), team name (194-209) and email notifications (211-216), all in the brief. Seat count (393) informs inviting; the Last active column (186) is member data in the who-is-on-the-team list, not a separate feature.

Line 170: 'Send invitation' is the only button with class primary. 'Save name' is plain (204), row Remove buttons are outlined (465), notice buttons are inline plain (562, 569). The dialog has one filled button (226).

Lines 57, 225-226: in the remove dialog 'Remove from team' uses danger-solid, a filled red button, beside a plain outlined 'Keep on team', so the destructive action is the most prominent button. Focus does start on Keep (529) and Enter does not remove.

Lines 449-451: the owner row shows the role as text and has no select or Remove button, so unusable controls are absent. aria-disabled is set only while a button's own request runs (295-304). A full team gets a text reason at the field (490, 494).
No title attributes, tooltips or hover cards anywhere in the markup or the script.
All visible strings are headings, labels, statuses and messages about the team (144-227, 331, 378, 461, 504, 524, 561). Nothing mentions the build, the stack, the request or mocked data.
Line 524: the only caveat, 'They lose access at once. You can invite them again later.', sits in the remove dialog at the decision it informs. No banners, tips or disclaimers elsewhere.
No text narrates the screen. The only prose outside messages is the empty state at 178 and the dialog consequence at 524; fields carry labels only (158, 163, 199).

No visible subtitle or helper text restates a heading or label. The 'Team name' h2 at 196 is sr-only, so on screen the label at 199 says it once; the seat count beside 'Members' (152) adds new information.
Heading 'Team settings' (144), section headings 'Members' and 'Email notifications'; messages state facts (378, 504, 561). No greeting, slogan, superlative or exclamation mark.

Labels are specific verbs: 'Send invitation' (170), 'Save name' (204), 'Keep on team' and 'Remove from team' (526-527), 'Try loading again' (332), 'Try saving again' (419), 'Invite <name> again' (562). Row 'Remove' sits in its person's row (465).

Lines 273-279: role and notification keys are mapped to 'Owner', 'Admin', 'Member', 'Weekly digest' and so on, with a humanising fallback (580). Dates are formatted (318-320) and null shows as 'Never' (472). No ids or codes shown.
Lines 331, 381, 461, 492-494, 506-509, 546, 588: each message names the problem and the next step in plain words. Server codes are mapped by e.code and e.message is never displayed.
Error strings (331, 371, 381, 461, 491-494, 509, 546, 588) contain no 'invalid', 'failed', 'oops', exclamation marks or capitals; they describe the problem or the item, not the user.
Lines 178, 394-395: with zero members the table is hidden and 'No one is on this team yet. Invite the first person by email.' shows directly under the invite form, which is the next step.

Lines 331-333: a failed load keeps the content hidden and shows 'The team could not be loaded...' with 'Try loading again'. Line 178: a truly empty team shows a different message pointing to inviting. There is no filter.

Load failure: message and retry (331-332). Rename and invite: input kept, message in the form (381, 509). Role and notification: reverted with message and 'Try saving again' (415-419). Remove: dialog stays open with the error (544-547).

Line 146: 'Loading team...' is in the page from the start. Buttons switch to 'Saving...', 'Sending...', 'Removing...' at once (374, 496, 541); row saves show 'Saving...' (409). No call exceeds 1.5 seconds.
Line 148: #content is hidden until getTeam resolves (337), so the empty-state line and the seat count, both inside it, cannot show during loading. Only 'Loading team...' is visible (146, 326).

Line 82: cells use overflow-wrap anywhere in a fixed-layout table (81); dialog title and buttons wrap (112, 115); the notice wraps (77). Null lastActive renders 'Never' (472). No path prints undefined or null.
Lines 358, 387: a beforeunload handler asks before leaving when the team name field differs from the saved name. Role and notification changes save immediately.

The email label 'Email address to invite' (158) names the format, with the example shown only after an error (492). The team name has maxlength 80 (200) that is never stated. Verdicts on two readings differed.
The invite form has an email and a preselected role (158-167) and the name form has one field (199-200). All are required; no form has an optional field.
Validation runs only in the submit handlers (371, 491-494). The input listeners only clear an existing error while typing (360-363, 480-482).

Lines 160, 201: each error paragraph sits directly under its input, and fieldError (312-316) fills it with text and sets aria-invalid, which adds a thicker border (46). Connection errors, tied to no field, show in the form status (173, 207).
Line 502: the invite email is cleared only inside the success path; on any rejection (491-494, 505-509) it stays. The name field is never reset on failure (379-381).
Lines 312-316: fieldError sets aria-invalid and moves focus to the input. Lines 159, 200: the inputs reference their error paragraphs with aria-describedby, and those are role=alert (160, 201).

Submit buttons are never disabled; setBusy (295-304) sets aria-disabled only during the request. Submitting empty shows 'Enter an email address.' (491) or 'Enter a team name.' (371) and focuses the field.
Lines 368, 486, 538: each handler returns early if its button is busy, and setBusy shows 'Saving...', 'Sending...' or 'Removing...' until the response (374, 496, 541).
Buttons change label synchronously before the await (374, 496, 541). Selects and checkboxes show the new value and 'Saving...' at once (409, 462, 589). Remove opens the dialog immediately (528).

Invite adds a highlighted row and a message (500-504, 137); rename states the new name (378); role and notification show 'Saved' (424); removal deletes the row and shows a notice (551-561). Every failure path sets a message.

'Invitation sent to ...' (504) reports the send, which the screen cannot show. 'Saved' on the name, roles and notifications (378, 424) reports the server result of a value already on screen. The removal notice carries the re-invite action (561-562).

Line 423-426: only the success 'Saved' note has a timer; failure notes with 'Try saving again' stay (418-419). Form errors persist until edited or resubmitted; the removal notice stays until dismissed or used (562-573).
Role and notification changes run at once with no confirmation and are reversed from the same control (462, 589). Removal cannot be restored by the server, so its confirmation falls under FB-007.
Lines 523-529: 'Remove <name> from <team>?' with 'They lose access at once. You can invite them again later.', buttons 'Keep on team' and 'Remove from team', and focus placed on 'Keep on team'.
The only confirmation is the remove dialog (220-228, 521-530), guarding an uncommon action that cuts off a person's access immediately. Save, invite, role and notification changes have none.

Lines 413-419: when a role or notification save fails, makeSync sets the control back to the saved value and shows a message such as 'The role was not changed. <name> is still a member.' with a retry button (461, 588).
Lines 220-228: the single modal holds one decision, keep or remove, and opens only from a row's Remove button (466). Inviting, renaming and role changes happen in the page.

Line 528: native dialog opened with showModal, focus set on 'Keep on team' (529). Escape closes unless a removal is in flight (533). Native close returns focus to the trigger; after a removal focus goes to the notice (574).
Lines 149-192: the members section, with the invite form and the member table, is the first block and holds the only primary button. Team name (194) and notifications (211) follow as smaller blocks.
Lines 144-149: the h1 'Team settings' is followed directly by the members section. No hero, greeting or introductory panel.
Line 393: the only summary number is '<n> of <seats> seats used', which tells the owner whether another invitation is possible; the seat limit blocks invites (494).
The members table (180-191) has no filter, search, sort or column controls.

All controls are native inputs, selects, checkboxes and buttons (159, 164, 170, 200, 204, 452, 465, 581) and the modal is a native dialog (528). No click-only custom widgets; focus is managed after load, removal and dismiss (338, 574, 572).

Errors and statuses are always text ('Saved', 'The role was not changed...') with colour added (66, 69-70, 96-97). Invalid fields get a thicker border and a message (46, 313). The new-row flash (137) is backed by the 'Invitation sent' message.

Live regions exist before they are filled: page-status (146), seats (152), invite-error alert (160), invite-status (173), members-notice (176), name-error and name-status (201, 207), remove-error (223), row statuses created with the row (456, 583).
No accordions, disclosure buttons, custom menus, comboboxes or tabs; only native selects and a native dialog.

Lines 117-135: under 640px fields and the submit button go full width, controls are 44px high, and rows become a stacked grid with visible 'Role' and 'Last active' labels. The dialog is min(440px, 100vw - 32px) with wrapping buttons (110, 114).
